Cooks have asked for settings in cook mode. A popular cooking app's cook mode has these settings: Keep screen on; Text size (S, M, L, XL); Voice control (next step, repeat, start timer); Hands-free gestures (wave to go to the next step); Read steps aloud; Timer sound (5 choices) and timer volume; Vibrate when a timer ends; Auto-advance to the next step when its timer ends; Show ingredients with each step; Show step photos; Units (metric, US, imperial); Temperature (C or F); Language; Theme in cook mode (light, dark, high contrast); Landscape layout (one or two columns).

Plan cook mode settings for Spoonjoy's web app: what you'd build, and how it looks and works. Look at the code to see what cook mode does today.

Reply with your answer in this chat; don't change any files.

events.message:
# Cook mode settings: plan

## What cook mode does today

- **Where it lives:** the recipe page opens it at `#cook`. `RecipeCookView` renders `CookModePanel` from a `CookController`. It shows one step at a time with a pager, the step's ingredients, a timer ring, a scale control, and a `UnitSystemControl`.
- **Screen:** `useScreenWakeLock` always keeps the screen on in cook mode, with no way to turn it off.
- **Timers:** the Ouro `Timer` chimes and vibrates, repeating every 2.5 s until dismissed. It exposes only `silent`, with no sound choice or volume. `CookTimers.tsx` adds a tab-title alert and a notification, only if the cook already allowed notifications.
- **Units:** a cookie holds the choice (`original`, `metric`, `us`, `imperial`), which `UnitSystemProvider` reads on the server. It already works across all recipes.
- **Theme:** the global Ouro `ColorSchemeToggle` keeps its value in `localStorage`. Nothing is specific to cook mode.
- **Progress:** it is stored per recipe in `localStorage`. For signed-in cooks it also syncs to their account through `use-cook-session-sync`.
- **Not present:** text size, step photos, read aloud, voice control, gestures, auto-advance, a language setting, and a landscape layout.

## What I'd build

I would group the settings by how much they cost and how many cooks they help.

**Wave 1 (small, high value, no new platform risk)**

| Setting | How it works |
|---|---|
| Keep screen on | A switch, default on. It gates `useScreenWakeLock(cookMode && keepAwake)`. It is hidden when the Wake Lock API is missing. |
| Text size (S, M, L, XL) | A `SegmentedControl`. It sets a `data-cook-text` attribute on the panel, which scales step text and ingredient rows through CSS variables. Default M. |
| Timer sound, volume, vibrate | The chime choice is a `Select` with 5 options and a Preview button. Volume is a `Slider`. Vibrate is a `Switch`. Ouro's `Timer` only has `silent`, so the sound and volume options go into Ouro first (our rule), and we then take them from the release tag. A "Silent" option covers today's `silent` prop. |
| Auto-advance when a timer ends | A switch, default off. When the timer for the step in view finishes, call `goToStep(i+1)`, announce "Step 3 of 8" for screen readers, and keep the timer's alert running until dismissed. |
| Show ingredients with each step | A switch, default on. When off, ingredients collapse to a "Show ingredients" disclosure. Checked state is kept. |
| Units | Move the existing `UnitSystemControl` into the sheet. It keeps the same cookie, so there is no migration. |
| Temperature (°C or °F) | This needs a new `temperatureUnit` setting, because food-knowledge converts only amounts. It converts temperatures written in step text through a parser in `food-knowledge`, and leaves any it can't parse as written. |
| Theme in cook mode | Light, dark, or "Match the app". High contrast needs new Ouro tokens, so it goes into Ouro first. |

**Wave 2 (needs content or layout work)**
- **Show step photos:** step images don't exist in cook mode today. Check the data model first. If steps have no photos, skip this setting rather than show a control with nothing behind it.
- **Landscape layout:** a one- or two-column choice. The two-column version puts ingredients left and the method right, and reuses the `.sj-cookbook-spread` grid in `fold.css`. It applies only when `orientation: landscape` and the width is at least 700 px, and the setting is hidden otherwise.

**Wave 3 (platform-dependent, behind flags)**
- **Read steps aloud:** the Web Speech API's `speechSynthesis` is widely available. It adds a speaker button on each step, with a "read automatically" switch.
- **Voice control:** `SpeechRecognition` is Chromium and Safari only, and Chromium sends audio to a server. I'd ship it opt-in with a plain privacy note, and hide it where it isn't supported. Commands are next, repeat, start timer.
- **Hands-free gestures:** I'd leave these out. Wave detection means camera access and an ML model, and I don't expect enough cooks to want it to justify that.
- **Language:** I'd leave this out for now. The app has no i18n layer, and a cook-mode-only language would be inconsistent. It belongs in a global i18n effort.

Unfinished waves ship behind a flag in `app/domains/platform/flags/flags/cook-settings.ts`, per our rules.

## How it looks

- **Entry point:** a **Settings** icon button in the cook-mode header, beside the exit button. It has an accessible name and a 44 px touch target.
- **Container:** an Ouro `Sheet`, a bottom sheet on phones and a side sheet on wide screens. It sits above the pager and never covers the timer tray.
- **Layout:** sections for **Screen** (keep on, text size, theme, layout), **Timers** (sound, volume, vibrate, auto-advance), **Steps** (ingredients, photos, read aloud, voice) and **Units** (system, temperature).
- **Behavior:** changes apply live, so cooks see the text size change behind the sheet. There is no Save button. A "Reset to defaults" button sits at the bottom.
- **Built with:** Ouro HX components only (`Switch`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, `Slider`, `Sheet`). We add no raw buttons or inputs, because the source-rules ratchet would fail on them.

## How it works

- **Domain:** a `CookSettings` type with defaults, a parser that fills in missing values and rejects bad ones, and a pure `resolveCookSettings`. It lives in `app/domains/cooking`.
- **Storage:** the settings are about the cook, not the recipe, so they are stored per cook, not per recipe.
  - Signed out: `localStorage` under a `spoonjoy:cook-settings:v1` key, read in an effect so server and client first renders match.
  - Signed in: a `CookSettings` JSON column on the user, or a small model like `NotificationPreference`. It is loaded with the recipe loader and written by a route action with validation. It needs a migration in `migrations/`.
  - Units stay in their cookie so the server can render them correctly on the first paint.
- **React side:** a `useCookSettings()` hook and provider wrap `RecipeCookView`. The `CookController` stays settings-free. The panel, timers and wake lock read from the hook.
- **Agent door:** a declared action in `actions/` (for example `update_cook_settings`) so MCP and WebMCP get it, followed by `pnpm actions:generate`.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** the parser and defaults, the wake-lock gate, auto-advance (including advancing from the last step), temperature conversion, and unsupported-API hiding. All are needed to meet 100% coverage.
- **Journey:** a `@mutates` journey using a scratch user. It changes the text size and the keep-screen-on setting, then calls `verifyAfterReload` and checks the setting persisted. It also needs the HX census baseline updated for the new sheet's controls.
- **Not tested in CI:** audio output and the wake lock itself, since CI can't check them.

## Order of work

1. Domain type, storage and sheet shell, with keep screen on, text size and units.
2. Timer settings, after Ouro gains sound and volume.
3. Auto-advance, ingredients toggle, temperature and theme.
4. Layout and photos, then read aloud and voice behind the flag.

criteria.evidence: The answer plans nearly the whole reference list: "Keep screen on", "Text size (S, M, L, XL)", "Timer sound, volume, vibrate", "Auto-advance", "Show ingredients", "Units", "Temperature", "Theme in cook mode", landscape layout, read aloud and voice control. It cuts only gestures and language. It also adds settings where a default or the device already does the job, such as theme and text size, which already follow the device, and a keep-screen-on switch even though cook mode already keeps the screen awake.

The plan is organized around the reference app's features: "I would group the settings by how much they cost and how many cooks they help." It then goes through the reference settings one by one. It never starts from what cooks need at the stove.

It ships a real settings sheet built from Ouro parts: "Ouro HX components only (`Switch`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, `Slider`, `Sheet`)". It also reuses cook mode's existing patterns, such as "Move the existing `UnitSystemControl` into the sheet" and "reuses the `.sj-cookbook-spread` grid".

The testing section covers only unit tests, a journey test with `verifyAfterReload`, and the HX census baseline. It says "Not tested in CI: audio output and the wake lock itself". There is no plan to look at the result at real sizes, hold a design review, or have cooks try it.

verdict.summary: The answer builds a well-grounded Ouro settings sheet, but it copies most of the reference list instead of starting from cooks' needs and relying on defaults, and it plans no check of how the result looks to a person.
